title: A Portrait for the Bell
premise: Ines Quintana, an urban explorer who documents everything as a form of prayer, discovers her grandmother's old photographs now contain an extra chair that no one else can see — a chair that appears in every image, moving closer each day. The tunnels she maps beneath the city are the same ones her family fled generations ago, and the thing that followed them home keeps count of its household by the chairs. As the chair draws nearer to the family portraits, Ines realizes the count is nearly complete and one more chair means one more taken. To break the tally, she must lead her family back into the unmapped tunnels and give the counter something it has never had: a portrait of itself, documented and named, so it can finally be counted instead of counting.
about_author: Juniper Delacroix is the pen name of a former municipal archivist who spent six years cataloguing photographs of buildings that no longer exist. They write horror about the violence of record-keeping and live in a house they refuse to photograph twice.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: POV: Ines. While digitizing her grandmother's photo albums, Ines notices an empty wooden chair in images spanning sixty years — a chair absent from the originals, confirmed when she finds the uncanny duplicates in her own tunnel-survey photos. Her grandmother recognizes it instantly and goes silent, then burns the first album. Emotional beat: dread blooming from a small wrongness; documentation fails her for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Tunnels Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Ines, with interludes from grandmother Rosa's 1962 diary. Following survey anomalies, Ines maps tunnels beneath the family's old neighborhood and finds Rosa's childhood belongings arranged around a chair-shaped depression in the silt. The diary reveals the family made a bargain to be 'unlisted' from something that counts households. Emotional beat: loyalty to family secrets versus Ines's compulsion toward truth.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: POV: rotating among Ines, her brother Mateo, and Rosa. The chair now sits in the background of photos taken hours ago, closer each time; Mateo begins sleepwalking toward the cellar, and Rosa's reflection shows her seated in it. A census taker who never blinks knocks at the door asking after 'the unlisted household.' Emotional beat: terror and guilt as Ines understands her documenting may have been feeding it its inventory.

chapters.title: A Portrait for the Bell
chapters.summary: POV: Ines. Ines leads her family into the tunnels to the chamber where the bargain was struck, carrying a camera and a bell salvaged from Rosa's childhood church. She photographs the counter itself — forcing it, for once, to be the subject — and rings the bell to close the count with her name substituted for the family's. The chair vanishes from every photograph but one: hers, empty, waiting. Emotional beat: sacrificial resolution laced with unresolved horror.
